newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OKs group formed to share fishing quota.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OKs group formed to share fishing quota.

text.p: The Justice Department on Tuesday approved a plan by four seafood fishing and processing companies to allocate among themselves the fixed quota of Pacific Whiting allowed to the group by the U.S. government.
The agency said the plan by the group known as the Whiting Conservation Cooperative was not anti-competitive.
The four members, Alaska Ocean Seafood, American Seafoods, Glacier Fish Co and Tyson Foods Inc's Seafood Group, are licensed to catch and process the Pacific Whiting fish.

The Commerce Department limits the amount of Pacific Whiting that may be harvested from U.S. waters annually for environmental and economic reasons. The agency also divides the total quota among three groups of processors.
The four companies will divide among themselves the 34 percent allotted by the Commerce Department to a group of catcher/processors.

The majority of each year's catch, 42 percent, is allocated to onshore processing plants. The remaining 24 percent is earmarked for ships that have on-board processing capabilities but do not catch the fish.
Pacific Whiting is used mostly to produce a protein paste known as surimi, which is sold to U.S. consumers as artificial crab meat or exported to Japan.
